label: Law firm
recognise: Law firms, solicitors, barristers, attorneys, notaries, immigration and legal advisers.
research: What websites of similar law firms (same practice areas and, if given, the same city) usually show, and what clients look for before they get in touch.

pages.title: Home
pages.purpose: The firm's practice areas, why clients choose it, and a clear way to book a consultation.

pages.title: About the firm
pages.purpose: The firm's history, values and how it works with clients.

pages.title: Practice areas
pages.purpose: Each area of law the firm handles, and the kinds of matters in each.

pages.title: Our team
pages.purpose: The lawyers with their roles, admissions and specialisms.

pages.title: Contact
pages.purpose: How to book a consultation, phone, email, office address and hours.

pages.title: Privacy policy
pages.purpose: How enquiries and personal information are handled and kept confidential.

pages.title: Legal disclaimer
pages.purpose: That the site's content is general information, not legal advice, and contacting the firm doesn't create a client relationship.

sections.header: The firm's name or logo, the main pages and a Book a consultation button.
sections.footer: Office address, phone, email, hours, practice areas, the privacy policy and the legal disclaimer.
sections.homepage: An assured, professional hero with what the firm does and a consultation button; the practice areas; why clients choose the firm; the team, only when the owner named them; how a first consultation works; a final call to get in touch.

rules: Never promise results or quote past case outcomes the owner didn't give.
State that the site's content is general information and not legal advice.
Admissions, accreditations, fees and awards only as the owner gives them.
Plain English over legal jargon; explain terms clients may not know.
A confident, sober look: strong type, restrained colour, generous spacing.

demo.note: Where the owner gave no details, write these as samples for them to replace. Samples are only ever offerings like these: never sample people, staff photos, opening hours, prices, addresses or phone numbers.

questions.title: Which areas of law do you handle?
questions.lead: The ones you want most enquiries for, first.
questions.why: The Practice areas page and the homepage lead with them.

questions.title: How does a first consultation work?
questions.lead: This sets the button in your header.
questions.why: It sets the button in your header.

questions.title: Where can clients reach you?
questions.lead: These go in your site details, the footer and the Contact page.
questions.why: Only you know your office address and numbers.

questions.title: Should the site show your lawyers?
questions.lead: Clients like to know who they'll work with.
questions.why: The Our team page needs them.

questions.title: What should it look and feel like?
questions.lead: The feel sets the colours; your logo makes it yours.
questions.why: Your logo and photos make the site yours.
